first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because Mykonos is on the family's list. The first screen is calm. It starts with areas, guest numbers and how people move around, and nothing is shouting. She kept going because the key takeaways say 800. Her summary: Saint John says up to 800, Petasos and the Myconian ballroom in Elia can take a few hundred, the Elia kitchens are halal certified, ZeNIT mentions security and transfers by sea, and almost nobody says whether a property can be closed. I read the Elia entry and the ZeNIT entry myself.

journey.section: Intro
journey.quote: The right one depends on how many guests you are inviting, the ceremony you want and how your guests will move around the island.
journey.reaction: Guest numbers and movement come first. It's the right order, and it isn't trying to sell me a sunset.

journey.section: Key takeaways
journey.quote: Guest count narrows the list quickly, because published capacity runs from 25 guests inside the Mykonos Grand chapel to weddings of up to 800 at Saint John.
journey.reaction: 800. This was the line that kept my assistant reading. On this island, a guest list our size is not out of the question.

journey.section: Capacity, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: For every other venue here, ask whether the wedding spaces, or the whole property, can be closed to other guests.
journey.reaction: That is my first question, put almost the way I would put it. They know there is a difference between a private terrace and a closed hotel.

journey.section: Resort, boutique hotel or event venue
journey.quote: If you are weighing a resort package against a venue on its own terms, our guide to [Greece wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) sets out how they compare.
journey.reaction: A link to packages just as I'm deciding what kind of place I want. This is where I feel filed as a standard client.

journey.section: 2. Katikies Mykonos, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: Children above 13 are welcome, and younger children are directed to the sister property, Katikies Villas Mykonos at Elia beach.
journey.reaction: Useful to know early. Our family has small children, and I won't split them off to another beach. Together with 50 seated, this is not for us.

journey.section: 3. Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: **Standout:** An open-air amphitheatre, and a complimentary evening shuttle to Mykonos Town for guests who want a night in town.
journey.reaction: A free shuttle as a standout. My guests won't be on a hotel shuttle. That's a detail for a holiday, not for a wedding like ours.

journey.section: 4. Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: **Standout:** The scale. Up to 800 guests is the largest published figure on this list.
journey.reaction: Said plainly, with no excitement. Good. But the rooms and exclusive use are not published, so I still don't know who else would be at the hotel.

journey.section: 6. Petasos Beach Resort & Spa, Platis Gialos
journey.quote: **Capacity:** The Swimming Pool takes 280 for a banquet, 350 for a reception and 500 for cocktails; the V.I.P. Restaurant 180, 220 and 300; Le Club Restaurant 70, 90 and 110.
journey.reaction: Real figures for each space and layout. My events team can start working from this.

journey.section: 7. Myconian Ambassador, Platis Gialos
journey.quote: **Standout:** Efisia, the hotel's fine-dining restaurant, and a team that presents itself "as experts in romance and discretion".
journey.reaction: Discretion is the word I look for. But this is the small one, so it's the right idea at the wrong size.

journey.section: 8. Royal Myconian and Myconian Imperial, Elia
journey.quote: **Standout:** The Horizons Ballroom is semi-open, covered from above, with sliding doors onto a small balcony, and divides into four sections for a smaller dinner.
journey.reaction: Covered and semi-open, so it works in the heat and the wind. It also divides, so a family dinner and the main night can use the same space.

journey.section: 8. Royal Myconian and Myconian Imperial, Elia
journey.quote: The kitchens are certified halal and kosher, and a South Asian chef cooks traditional Indian cuisine.
journey.reaction: This is the line my assistant would underline and send to my mother. Certified halal is not a detail for us. It decides whether the family comes.

journey.section: 8. Royal Myconian and Myconian Imperial, Elia
journey.quote: For a multi-day celebration or a multicultural wedding, the halal, kosher and Indian kitchens are worth a close look.
journey.reaction: Cultural needs, said without stereotyping, plus 'multi-day'. Someone has thought about weddings like ours.

journey.section: 10. ZeNIT Events Center, above Paradise beach
journey.quote: **On the day:** The venue's own services include a physician and medical room during events, security with CCTV, and guest transfers that ZeNIT runs itself for up to 16 guests, with larger groups handled through its partners and transfers by sea also offered.
journey.reaction: Security, a doctor on site and arrival by sea. This is the first time the page talks my language. My question is whether our own security team can work with theirs.

journey.section: 10. ZeNIT Events Center, above Paradise beach
journey.quote: **Rooms:** None. ZeNIT is an events venue, not a hotel.
journey.reaction: Then 300 guests sleep somewhere else and travel up a hill above Paradise beach. On Mykonos in summer, that is where phones and photographers get close.

journey.section: Getting to Mykonos for your wedding
journey.quote: From the airport, a bus runs to Mykonos Town (Chora) and other destinations from a stop in front of the terminal in the Arrivals area, with tickets bought from the driver.
journey.reaction: Buying bus tickets from the driver. Nothing on private cars, meet-and-greet or private aircraft. My assistant would cut this whole section from her summary.

journey.section: When to marry in Mykonos
journey.quote: Agree a covered or indoor fallback with your venue in advance; Saint John, the Myconian Collection and ZeNIT all publish indoor or covered spaces.
journey.reaction: Heat and wildfire are covered calmly, with a plan and with names attached. My security team would want this.

journey.section: When to marry in Mykonos
journey.quote: Smartraveller also advises care when swimming because of boat traffic, coastal hazards, strong currents and marine life, and suggests patrolled beaches where possible.
journey.reaction: Government advice on patrolled beaches. Fine for a backpacker, but it's not why I'm reading.

journey.section: Getting married legally in Mykonos
journey.quote: **Proving you are free to marry.** As at November 2026, Smartraveller says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most often with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and registry certificates.
journey.reaction: Our lawyers handle this, and we are not only Australian. Skipped.

journey.section: Shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The next step is finding out which of them are free on your date, on your terms.
journey.reaction: 'On your terms' is the right note. It's quiet and not eager.

journey.section: Shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person from start to finish is what I want. 'For Australian couples' makes me wonder if my family is the client they had in mind.

unanswered_questions: Can Saint John, Petasos or the Myconian Elia hotels be closed to the public for three days or more for 200 to 400 guests?
How many rooms does Saint John have, and could our whole guest list stay there?
Can the Horizons Ballroom and the beach be used across several days for different ceremonies and family customs?
Can our own security team work with the venue's, and how are vendors, staff phones and guest photography controlled to keep the wedding out of the press?
Can private cars, meet-and-greet at Mykonos Airport, private aviation and sea transfers be arranged for every guest, not only at ZeNIT?
Have they delivered a wedding of 200 to 400 guests on Mykonos, and is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you are weighing a resort package against a venue on its own terms, our guide to [Greece wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) sets out how they compare.
turn_offs_found.why: It comes right where I'm choosing the kind of place I want, and it treats packages as the default way to compare. That is how a standard client is handled, and being treated as a standard client is one of my main fears.

turn_offs_found.quote: **Standout:** An open-air amphitheatre, and a complimentary evening shuttle to Mykonos Town for guests who want a night in town.
turn_offs_found.why: Calling a free shuttle a standout is value talk. It suggests the reader counts what's included, when I'm judging whether a venue can manage private movement for VIP guests.

turn_offs_found.quote: From the airport, a bus runs to Mykonos Town (Chora) and other destinations from a stop in front of the terminal in the Arrivals area, with tickets bought from the driver.
turn_offs_found.why: Explaining bus tickets, followed by beach-safety advice, pitches the arrival section at an ordinary holidaymaker. It says nothing about private logistics, and that is exactly what I would judge a planner on.

would_share_with: My assistant, to approach Saint John, Petasos and the Myconian Elia hotels about full closure, room counts and multi-day use
My mother, for the halal-certified kitchens and the covered Horizons Ballroom
Our head of security, for the ZeNIT entry (CCTV, physician, sea transfers)

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet, with no prices or bargain talk, and I prefer that. But I don't fill in web forms, and nothing on the page shows they have handled a wedding our size. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Rework 'Getting to Mykonos' so it doesn't read as public transport first (bus tickets from the driver, the taxi stand). Cover private options instead (private cars, meet-and-greet, private aviation, sea transfers), but only where they can be confirmed. ZeNIT's sea transfers are already sourced and could be mentioned here.

Remove the 'resort package' link from the 'Resort, boutique hotel or event venue' section, and drop 'complimentary evening shuttle' from the Mykonos Grand standout. Both make the page read like a list of tiers and inclusions.

Add one short line to the capacity section that groups the large-wedding options already on the page: Saint John up to 800, Petasos 280 to 500, Horizons Ballroom 270 to 550, ZeNIT's security and sea transfers. Then a large family can see its path without reading all ten entries.
